newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Time Warner stock jumps after results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Time Warner stock jumps after results.

text.p: Time Warner Inc's first-quarter results on Wednesday gave the first hint of how the Turner Broadcasting System merger might benefit the company, and eager investors scooped up the shares in response.

Analysts said it appeared Time Warner was finding a way to make its wide array of media properties work together, producing increased cash flow that could eventually pay down debt, which has been troublesome to some investors.
Analysts said the increase in operating cash flow offered the best evidence that Time Warner was on track to reduce its debt, which some consider too high at the current $17.5 billion.
"It means they can generate free cash flow. There are a lot of implications with that message," Merrill Lynch analyst Jessica Reif said. "It's just a sign they're finally working as one company."
Even excluding the Turner properties and other acquisitions, first-quarter operating cash flow grew by about 16 percent compared with the same period last year.
Further confidence was fueled by Chairman and Chief Executive Gerald Levin's expectation that the company would post double-digit growth in EBITDA in the coming year.
Time Warner said its first-quarter net loss narrowed to $43 million, or $0.08 per share, from a net loss of $153 million, or $0.39. Revenues rose to $3.03 billion from $2.07 billion.
Analysts on average expected the company to post a loss of $0.32 per share in the latest quarter, according to First Call.
Time Warner now consists of film, cable, television and other entertainment divisions. The goal is to have all of those pieces working together to cross-promote the various products and programs.
"There's evidence there is some of the synergy they've talked about for years," A.G. Edwards analyst Michael Kupinski said.
